triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix entry-level rate applied the full forced-labor section 301 overlay rate to entries of humanitarian-donation articles (HTS 9903.05.91) and informational-material articles (HTS 9903.05.92), although both headings provide only "The duty provided in the applicable subheading" and therefore exempt such entries from the additional duty.
triage.triage_notes: Single-module commit (index 0 is the only module file; companion test us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-duty/composition.test.yaml plus the encoding manifest and provisions reverse index are the other changed files). The module is format: rulespec/v1 with module.kind: composition, i.e. an assembled pipeline module, but it does define derived rules with formulas, so the change is a genuine formula-meaning change rather than a compose-spec/config edit. Decisive hunk adds `or entry_is_humanitarian_donation_article or entry_is_informational_material_article` to the effective_from 2026-07-24 version of forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate; both facts already existed in the module pre-fix (used by entry_is_fentanyl_canada_excepted / entry_is_fentanyl_mexico_excepted at lines 1274 and 1303 of the parent file), so no new inputs or outputs were introduced. Provisions were read through the pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union: 9903.05.91 = "Articles that are donations by persons subject to the jurisdiction of the United States, such as food, clothing and medicine, intended to be used to relieve human suffering" and 9903.05.92 = "Articles that are informational materials, ...", each with "Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading" - confirming they are exceptions to the overlay, so the zero branch is correct. Note the resolver reported fix_time_corpus_match = provision_file_absent_at_corpus_ref and fell back to a later release (fallback_index 16); the excerpt text matches the proof atoms verbatim, so this does not change the reading. The rest of the diff is provenance/prose: two added source_verification citation paths in each of the two lists, two new verbatim exception proof atoms, an updated `source:` string, and reworded module notes/summary - mechanical on their own, but they accompany the substantive formula fix. PR #1196 has no review text in the bundle (reviews, review_comments, issue_comments all empty); the only quotable evidence is the commit message, which names the defect exactly.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes encoded meaning inside `rules[forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate].versions[1].formula`, adding two disjuncts to the zero branch so that humanitarian-donation and informational-material entries no longer receive the forced-labor overlay rate; effective dates, version windows, parameter values, entity, and rule count (49 rule declarations both pre and post) are unchanged. The pre-fix rule already declared itself the "Legally complete forced labor section 301 component" and already carried the proof atom quoting "Except as provided in headings 9903.05.85–9903.06.21", a range that contains 9903.05.91 and 9903.05.92, so this is a missing source-stated exception rather than new coverage the module never claimed. Reading both headings through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03, provision file sha 7406b42f…) confirms each provides only "Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading", i.e. no additional duty, and their text matches the added excerpts verbatim. The two consumed facts (`entry_is_humanitarian_donation_article`, `entry_is_informational_material_article`) already existed in the module as free variables of the fentanyl exception rules at pre-fix lines 1274/1303, so no input or output surface was expanded — only a wrong result was corrected.
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "enhancement, not defect" — rejected, because the pre-fix `source:` string and module notes both asserted the rule was the *legally complete* entry-level rate for the family, so omission contradicts the module's own claim; (2) "new outputs/scope" — rejected, rule-declaration count is 49 in both revisions, the ledger is unchanged (+0/-0 per commit body), and both facts were already consumed elsewhere in the module; (3) alternative kinds — amount_mismatch fails (the 0.10/0.125 tier parameters are untouched), boundary_direction and polarity_or_logic fail (the or-chain's form was correct, it was simply short two disjuncts, nothing inverted), untraceable_branch fails (nothing removed or re-grounded), wrong_period_or_effective_date fails (effective_from 2026-07-24 unchanged), wrong_entity_or_scope fails (entity CustomsEntry, period Day unchanged). One unrelated observation for the reviewer: the pre-existing proof atom cited to `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-553` resolves in the pinned release to reciprocal-tariff rows (9903.02.02–9903.02.05), not the forced-labor U.S. note 52 text it quotes — a pagination/citation-path drift that predates this commit and is independent of this fix. The panel-facing `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` was deliberately left at the non-exempt projection, consistent with the module notes.
